pure-announcement.rationale: It is a full product manual rather than launch or funding coverage, and it does describe transferable machinery — hook-based session capture, tiered consolidation with decay, RRF-fused hybrid retrieval — beyond the product pitch.

duplicate.rationale: No nearest concept covers persistent cross-session agent memory; 'Context layer' and 'Retrieval as composition' are enterprise context-infrastructure ideas, and the hybrid-retrieval overlap with 'Graph vs vector retrieval for code' is topical, not substantive.

unfalsifiable.rationale: Headline numbers are tied to a public dataset (LongMemEval-S) with an in-repo reproduction harness, and the note itself flags which competitor figures are unverified self-reports.

durability.rationale: The note is dominated by content the rubric names as perishable — benchmark pass rates, competitor star counts, model pricing at 2026-05-23, an engine pinned to v0.11.2, port tables, and workarounds for open upstream issues — with the durable memory-pipeline ideas a small fraction of it.

actionability.rationale: Nearly every instruction is wiring this product into one of thirty hosts; the transferable design guidance (capture via lifecycle hooks, compress, inject under a token budget) is present only as feature description, not as something a reader could build from.

atomicity.rationale: It interleaves at least two separable stories — the agent-memory system itself and the iii runtime platform pitch ('what iii replaces', its console and worker registry) — plus freestanding local-model cost guidance, so no single paragraph carries the note.
